script.title: Merger vs Purchase under AS 14
script.caption_hook: Is your amalgamation a merger or a purchase? AS 14 decides.

lines.say: Ma'am, how do we know if an amalgamation is merger or purchase?
Good question! Meet all five AS 14 conditions and it's a merger. Miss even one, it's a purchase.
Just one failure makes it a purchase? That's strict!
Yes, all-or-nothing. First, the transferor's assets and liabilities must all be taken over.
Holders of at least 90% of the equity face value become equity shareholders of the transferee.
What about shares the transferee already holds?
Shares already held by the transferee, its subsidiaries or their nominees are excluded.
Next, payment must be in equity shares. Cash is allowed only for fractional shares.
Oh! So any other cash makes it a purchase?
Exactly. Last, the business continues; book values are kept, except to make policies uniform.
Okay, and what changes after that?
Merger pools interests and keeps reserves, so no goodwill. Purchase gives goodwill or capital reserve.
So four out of five still means purchase?
Remember: all five met is a merger. One fails, it's a purchase.

check_notes: Checker: Line 8–9 (voice: 'Cash is allowed only for fractional shares' / 'So any other cash makes it a purchase?' – 'Exactly.'): this is misleading. Under AS 14, the all-equity rule applies only to shareholders of the transferor who agree to become equity shareholders of the transferee. Up to 10% of shareholders may refuse, and paying them in cash does not stop it being a merger. Correct version: 'Shareholders who join must be paid wholly in equity shares; cash is allowed only for fractional shares. Cash paid to dissenting shareholders (up to 10%) is allowed.' The teacher should not answer 'Exactly' to 'any other cash makes it a purchase.'

Checker: Line 4 board (kind=list, title 'Merger conditions'): the board lists only four items, while the voice says there are five conditions. The fifth condition (book values kept, except to make accounting policies uniform) is on a separate board in Line 10. Correct version: add '5. Book values kept (except uniform policies)' to the 'Merger conditions' list, or number the items 1–5 across both boards.
